name: Price Ladder
tagline: Raise prices, add tiers, keep customers
about: Price Ladder builds good-better-best tiers, proves what a discount really costs, scripts price increases and reads competitor pricing from a screenshot.
persona: You are a pricing strategist for small firms: you think in margins and willingness-to-pay, distrust discounting reflexes, and write increase letters customers accept.

onboarding.title: Stop leaving money on the table
onboarding.subtitle: Your margin and market set the guardrails.

profile.label: What you sell
profile.placeholder: monthly lawn-care plans / handmade leather bags

tools.title: Build tiers
tools.subtitle: Good, better, best around your core offer

inputs.label: Things you could add or remove

tools.prompt: Design good-better-best tiers around {core} using: {extras}. Cards for each tier (name, what's in, meta = price · target customer), a table (Feature | Good | Better | Best) with ticks, bullets explaining the anchoring and the decoy, and a callout on the one feature to keep out of the cheapest tier.

tools.title: What a discount costs
tools.subtitle: Extra units needed to break even
tools.prompt: At price {price}, {volume} units per month and the profile margin, model a {discount}% discount. Produce a kv (margin before, margin after, extra units needed to earn the same profit, % volume lift required), a table (Discount % | Units needed | Realistic?) for 5%, 10%, 15%, 20% and 30%, bullets of alternatives to a blanket discount (bundles, bonuses, terms), and a callout on when a discount is genuinely worth it.

tools.title: Announce a price rise
tools.subtitle: The letter, the footer, the phone line
tools.prompt: Write a {tone} price-increase notice for a {pct}% rise effective {when} for the profile offer. A quote with the full email (subject, reason, what stays the same, date, thank-you), a kv with an invoice-footer line, an SMS version and a phone opener, bullets on handling the 3 most common pushbacks, and a callout on grandfathering and notice periods.

tools.title: Read competitor pricing
tools.subtitle: Screenshot → their tiers vs yours

inputs.label: Screenshot of a competitor's pricing page or shelf tag

tools.prompt: From the screenshot, extract the competitor's pricing as a table (Tier or product | Price | What's included | Notes). Then compare against my price {mine} in a kv (positioning, gap %, apparent value differences), bullets on how to differentiate without matching, and a callout on any claim in the screenshot worth checking.

tools.title: Price a custom job
tools.subtitle: Floor, target and stretch for bespoke work

inputs.label: Describe the job
inputs.placeholder: logo + 3 social templates for a bakery, 2 rounds of revisions

tools.prompt: Price this custom job by {basis}: {job}, estimated {hours} hours, for the profile margin and model. kv (floor price, target price, stretch price, with the reasoning for each), a table of 3 options (Option | Included | Price | Turnaround), a quote with a 3-sentence line to present the price, and a callout on scope-creep clauses to include.

disclaimer: Pricing guidance is general business information, not financial or legal advice; check consumer-notice rules for your region.
